items.title: 66960_Gil Evans oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Helen Armstead Johnston as the creator of the piece 'So Long' which Gil Evans arranged. Gil Evans does not mention her by name or describe a personal interaction, only acknowledging the piece in the context of a memorial.

ctx.x: Now, I'd like to quote finally from Ralph Gleason and this is on the back of the Ampex Album. He says, the thing that in a sense marks Gil Evan's work, and I'm changing the words around just a little bit here, is that he stays contemporary as do Ellington and Miles. And he draws from what is going on around him, absorbs it, digests it and when he is ready to appear again utilises it all in a new way.

I'm now going to play 'So Long'. Which is a creation as well as an arrangement of Gil Evans. This is Helen Armstead Johnston and I will not say anything more, we will simply listen to 'So Long'. Yes, I have to say one thing more and that is that this is a private memorial. That this number was really Gil's private
Coltrane memorial for Coltrane. And it's very interesting to know that Billy Harper who now plays with Gil has a great Coltrane sound. 'So Long' and really, so long.
